subject: Mid-cycle initiative triage + runway asks
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-cycle initiative triage + runway asks

Team —

Quick mid-cycle check as we prep the QBR: overall OKR health is mixed and we need a short set of decisions so we can finalize the QBR narrative and commit runway. High-level: token-cost initiatives are on track, but infra/cost optimizations and 99th latency work are behind plan and require either added headcount or scope changes.

Summary (high level):
- On track: embeddings infra, inference pricing experiments.
- At risk: 99th-pctl latency improvements (infra + kernel work), cache reuse for bursty traffic, and A/B rollout automation for Dedicated customers.

Concrete asks:
1) Decide whether to re-scope "99th-pctl latency" from committed -> stretch (i.e., leave as high-priority but not required for Q3 target) or keep as committed and approve hires.
2) If we keep it committed: approve 2 infra FTE (backend runtime) + 1 SRE contractor for 6 weeks starting Aug 2 to complete kernel tuning and canary infra changes.
3) Product / PMs: please identify any non-essential feature work that can be deferred by Jul 20 EOD to free 1.5 engineer-months.
4) Eng leads: send revised ETA and risk notes by end-of-day Jul 20 so Evelyn can fold into the QBR deck.

Attached: runway_estimates.xlsx (sheet: headcount-impact), current_initiatives.csv (live tracker).

Ask: call here — if we cannot get hires approved, I propose re-scoping 99th-latency to "stretch" and moving the A/B rollout automation to Q4. Please reply with your take or a short counterproposal.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
VP, Platform & Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle initiative triage + runway asks

Jonas —

Thanks for the clear asks. Short answer: I think we can avoid full hiring if we take a targeted approach. Notes below: 

- 99th-pctl latency: we can carve a reduced-scope plan that focuses on kernel selection and a hot-path optimization for long sequences. That should cover ~60% of the expected 99th improvements on a ~4 week timeline.
- Headcount alternative: propose 1 infra FTE (senior) + a specialized contractor (kernel optim) for 4 weeks. That reduces cost and gets meaningful lift.
- Deprioritization: suggest pushing back the non-blocking Dedicated UI polish and two low-impact telemetry features (see tracker rows 42-43).

I updated the shared QBR prep doc with the reduced-scope timeline and annotated the risk column (link in thread). If leadership wants the full committed OKR to stay, we do need the hires Jonas proposed. 

I'll get a short ETA table to Evelyn by EOD today.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Product Operations

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle initiative triage + runway asks

On Sat, Jul 18, 2026 at 11:05 AM Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com> wrote:
> - 99th-pctl latency: we can carve a reduced-scope plan...

Agree with Laura's narrower approach but a couple cautions from infra:
- If we cut caching rework, we risk higher tail costs under burst scenarios; that is where the real cost variance lives. I'd prefer we keep a minimal cache-safety effort in the plan.
- Suggested execution: two-phase plan -> Phase 1 (weeks 1-4): kernel opt + targeted hot-path; Phase 2 (weeks 5-8): cache reuse + canary infra (only if metrics meet phase 1). This keeps us flexible and reduces upfront hires.

I can scope the Phase 1 deliverables and resource map by Monday. Marcus

Marcus Lin
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: QBR draft + status snapshot (please confirm decisions)

Team —

I've pulled the inputs and drafted the QBR narrative reflecting the reduced-scope path (attached). Quick summary of the page that will go to execs:
- Recommendation: adopt Laura + Marcus two-phase reduced-scope with 1 infra FTE + 4-week kernel contractor. Treat 99th-pctl as "committed" for Phase 1 measurable targets and "stretch" for Phase 2 items pending metrics.
- Tradeoffs: modest risk to tail-cost iff cache work delayed; mitigations listed in slide 6.
- Ask: leadership confirmation by close of business Jul 22 so we can lock slides and share the QBR packet with Sales/CS.

Attachments (stubs): QBR-draft.deck.pdf (v0.6, includes slides + decisions), OKR-traffic-scenarios.csv (traffic sims used for impact table).

If I don't hear back, I'll present the recommendation above. If you have edits, add comments to the drive doc or reply here.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Product Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Anna Zhou <anna@horizon.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle initiative triage + runway asks

Jonas —

Thanks for the heads up and for looping us in. Horizon Analytics is fine pausing our planned integration tests until you confirm the routing/latency changes — we don't want to skew your measurements. We can hold off and run our end-to-end validation on Aug 3; please confirm the cutover window and whether you need test vectors from our side.

I'll coordinate internally and mark Aug 3 as tentative.

Best,
Anna Zhou
Director, Integrations
Horizon Analytics
